quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: Send and Void ignore network failure: fetch rejection is unhandled and the user sees nothing
evidence: Only !res.ok is handled (app.js:27, :34). A rejected fetch (offline, DNS, CORS, abort) throws inside the async handler with no try/catch, so it becomes an unhandled promise rejection and no alert is shown. The same applies to app.js:33. In addition tooSoon() has already consumed the 1 second window at guards.js:24. Traced.
failing_case: Go offline, click Send invoice. No message appears; console shows an uncaught TypeError: Failed to fetch. A retry within one second is also silently swallowed by tooSoon(). Sam believes the invoice may have been sent.
remediation: Wrap both fetch calls in try/catch, show the cause and next step in an alert region for rejections as well as non-2xx, and only start the throttle once a request is actually in flight.

title: Double-send guard is a 1 second timer, not an in-flight or idempotency guard: duplicate invoices on a slow network
evidence: app.js:25 calls tooSoon() then awaits fetch at app.js:26 with no pending flag, no disabled button, no idempotency key. Lines are never cleared after success (app.js:28). Any request slower than 1 second leaves the window open for a second POST of the same lines.
failing_case: Click Send at t=0; the API takes 3 seconds. Click Send again at t=1.2 s (user thinks nothing happened because nothing visibly changes). Two POST /api/invoices with identical bodies are sent, and the client is billed twice.
remediation: Disable the Send button and set an in-flight flag until the response settles, send an idempotency key per invoice, and clear or lock the lines after a confirmed success.

title: Price and quantity accept values that turn into Infinity and are sent as null
evidence: app.js:18-19: only `price > 0` and the digits regex are checked. Number("1e999") is Infinity and passes `price > 0`. validQuantity (guards.js:16) accepts a string of 400 digits, and Number() of it is Infinity. JSON.stringify(Infinity) is null (app.js:26). Number() also accepts "0x10" (=16) as a price. Traced from the ECMAScript semantics; node was not available to run it.
failing_case: Enter price `1e999`, quantity 1, Add line: the list shows `Infinity`, the total shows `Infinity`, and Send posts `[{"client":"a","qty":1,"price":null}]`. Price `0x10` is silently billed as 16.00.
remediation: One normaliser for money inputs: match /^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$/, reject non-finite results and set a maximum for price and quantity, then store the amount as integer cents.

quote: const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.qty * l.price, 0);
title: Money is summed as floats from unrounded prices: listed lines and the total can disagree, and Infinity is accepted
evidence: The price check at app.js:19 is only !(price > 0), so any precision and Infinity pass. Each line is displayed with price.toFixed(2) (app.js:8) but the total sums the raw qty*price (app.js:10). The raw floats are what is posted (app.js:26).
failing_case: Price 1.005, quantity 100: the line renders '100 × 1.00' (1.005 is stored as 1.00499...), the total renders 100.50 (100.49999999999999.toFixed(2)). The screen shows 100 × 1.00 = 100.50. Price '1e999' becomes Infinity: the line shows 'Infinity' and the total shows 'Infinity'. Price 0.004 gives lines displayed as 0.00 while the total grows.
remediation: Parse price at the boundary into integer cents (reject more than 2 decimals and non-finite values) and compute the total in one pure, tested function; display and send the same cent values.

title: Whitespace-only client passes the form's required check and adds a line with an empty client
evidence: index.html:14 uses the required attribute, which accepts '   '. The value is then trimmed to '' here, and app.js:19 never checks client. The line is pushed at app.js:20 and rendered as an empty link at app.js:8, and later sent in the invoice.
failing_case: Type three spaces in Client, quantity 1, price 5, press Add line. A blank line item is added, counted in the total, and sent to the server with client ''.
remediation: Validate the trimmed client in the handler (reject empty with an error message) or add a pattern attribute that rejects blank values.

title: Add line silently does nothing when quantity or price is invalid
evidence: app.js:19 returns with no message, no focus move, no aria-invalid and no text. index.html has no error element and styles.css has no invalid state. Traced.
failing_case: Type quantity `2.5` (or `0`, or `2 `+letters) and a price, press Add line: nothing is added and nothing is said. The same happens with an empty price. The user cannot tell which field is wrong or that anything failed.
remediation: Show a per-field error message linked with aria-describedby, set aria-invalid, move focus to the first bad field, and say the rule ("Quantity must be a whole number, 1 or more").

title: A successful send has no visible result, and sentCount is never read
evidence: On success the handler only increments sentCount. grep of app.js, index.html shows nothing reads sentCount. The line list and total stay exactly as before. Traced.
failing_case: Click Send with two lines; the request succeeds. Screen is unchanged, so Sam cannot tell it worked, clicks again after a second, and sends a duplicate.
remediation: Show a confirmation (what was sent, to whom, total) in a polite live region, clear or lock the lines, and remove the unused counter or display it.

title: Void is destructive with no confirmation, no success state and no target; it is styled identically to Send
evidence: The click fires the POST immediately for an admin. The request names no invoice. On success nothing is shown and the lines remain on screen (app.js:34 handles only failure). styles.css:4 gives both buttons the same look; index.html:23-24 places them adjacent.
failing_case: An admin aims for Send invoice, mis-clicks the adjacent Void invoice, and the invoice is voided at once with no prompt, no undo, and no on-screen sign that it happened.
remediation: Add a confirm step that names the invoice, send the invoice id in the request, show a success message and update the page state, and demote or separate Void visually from the primary action.

title: Void permission is enforced only in the browser, on a mutable page global
evidence: The only authorization check in the payload is canVoid(user) at app.js:32, reading a top-level const that the console can mutate. The void request at app.js:33 carries no user or invoice identity in the body. Server code is not in the payload, so server enforcement is unknown (q: does /api/invoices/void check the session role?).
failing_case: In the dev console type user.roles.push("admin") and click Void invoice. canVoid now returns true and POST /api/invoices/void is sent. If the server trusts the client check, a viewer voids an invoice.
remediation: Enforce the admin rule on the server from the authenticated session. Treat the client check as UI hint only, and derive roles from the server response rather than a literal.

requirement.why: guards.js:9 comment says only admins may void; enforcement location inferred from the absence of any server code in the payload

title: Void invoice does nothing and says nothing for the signed-in user
evidence: app.js:2 sets user.roles to ["viewer","billing"]. guards.js:11 canVoid needs "admin". index.html:24 always renders the Void button, enabled. The handler at app.js:32 returns with no message, no disabled state, no aria feedback. Traced.
failing_case: Sam (viewer, billing) tabs to Void invoice and presses Enter. Nothing visible changes and no request is sent. Sam cannot tell whether the invoice was voided, refused, or the button is broken, and may press it repeatedly or assume it worked.
remediation: Do not render, or set disabled with an explanation, the Void button for users who cannot void. If the button stays visible, show a reason ('Only admins can void invoices') in a live region when the check fails.

title: Each line renders a link to "#" that goes nowhere
evidence: No click handler exists on the list (app.js has no listener on #lines). The anchor is a tab stop for every line, and the title duplicates the link text.
failing_case: Tab through a 20-line invoice: 20 extra tab stops. Press Enter on one: the page jumps to the top and appends '#' to the URL/history; no action occurs.
remediation: Render the client as plain text (or a real control with a handler); drop the redundant title.

title: Send invoice is allowed with no lines
evidence: No check on lines.length before the POST at app.js:26. With the initial empty array (app.js:1) the body is '[]'. index.html:23 renders Send enabled from first load.
failing_case: Open the page and click Send invoice. POST /api/invoices with body [] is sent; depending on the server, an empty invoice is created or a 4xx 'not sent' alert appears for something the UI should have prevented.
remediation: Disable Send until at least one line exists and show an empty state ('Add a line to start an invoice') in the list area.

title: Live region is rebuilt wholesale on every add, so screen readers can re-read the entire list
evidence: render() at app.js:7 replaces innerHTML of this list each time; every <li> is a new node and counts as an addition to a polite live region. Traced; not tested with a screen reader.
failing_case: With 20 lines entered, adding the 21st can make the reader announce all 21 rows again rather than only the new one.
remediation: Append only the new <li>, or announce a short status string ('Line added, total 42.00') in a separate live region.
